metadata.title: Referral pathways for ocular tumours
metadata.summary: This guidance sets out which ocular tumours warrant referral to designated ocular oncology services and which findings generally do not. It describes how to refer patients, what information to provide, and how MOLES scoring informs referral for melanocytic choroidal tumours. It is intended to support, rather than replace, ophthalmologists’ clinical judgment.

conditions_covered: Congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
Combined hamartoma of the retina and RPE
target_population: Adult patients with ocular tumours being considered for specialist referral

special_populations.population: Patients in Scotland with eyelid and orbital tumours
special_populations.considerations: Referral to the Scottish service is an option.
Referral to a centre other than Glasgow should occur only in exceptional circumstances and requires prior approval from National Services Division NHS Scotland.

document_sections.heading: 1. Introduction
document_sections.content: In 1997, the National Commissioning Group designated Liverpool, London and Sheffield as supraregional adult ocular oncology centres in England. Scotland’s National Services Division designated a Scottish service at North Glasgow University Hospital. This guidance is not prescriptive: it aims to improve adult referrals to designated centres for specialist care delivered remotely or in person. Referring ophthalmologists should use their clinical judgment, taking account of their expertise and each patient’s findings and circumstances.

document_sections.heading: Retinal/RPE tumours
document_sections.content: Refer patients with retinal haemangioblastoma, vasoproliferative tumour, vitreoretinal lymphoma, retinoblastoma, or retinocytoma / spontaneously regressed retinoblastoma.

document_sections.heading: Uveal tumours
document_sections.content: Refer a melanocytic choroidal tumour with a MOLES score of 3 or more, a choroidal haemangioma accompanied by subretinal fluid and/or symptoms, a choroidal osteoma, or lymphoma.

document_sections.heading: Iris Tumours
document_sections.content: Refer a melanocytic iris tumour if it has diameter > 5.0 mm, diffuse growth or seeding, secondary glaucoma or cataract, or angle involvement. Refer an iris cyst that threatens vision, for example because it is large or has documented growth.

document_sections.heading: Other tumours
document_sections.content: Refer any ciliary body tumour; any metastatic or paraneoplastic tumour requiring specialist ocular oncology; any suspected recurrence following treatment; and any other primary intraocular tumour for which an ocular oncology opinion is indicated.

document_sections.heading: Patients with conjunctival and epibulbar tumours
document_sections.content: Refer a nodular melanocytic tumour if it affects non-bulbar conjunctiva, grows after the teenage years, has diameter > 5 mm, has feeder vessels, or shows diffuse pigmentation. Refer primary acquired melanosis if it has grown recently, involves more than a third of the conjunctiva, or affects non-bulbar conjunctiva. Also refer squamous/sebaceous carcinoma, whether intraepithelial or invasive, lymphoma, and any suspected recurrence after treatment.

document_sections.heading: Retinal/RPE/ciliary epithelial tumours
document_sections.content: Do not refer astrocytic hamartoma(s) unless the diagnosis is uncertain. Retinal cavernous angioma, arteriovenous malformation, congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium, and combined hamartoma of the retina and RPE are also listed as conditions not to refer. The same list includes probable choroidal naevus with MOLES score <3; congenital ocular melanocytosis unless a tumour is present; melanocytoma of disc if less than 2 mm in thickness; choroidal haemangioma without serous retinal detachment; and iris arteriovenous malformation.

document_sections.heading: Conjunctival and adnexal tumours
document_sections.content: Do not refer complexion-associated melanosis. The non-referral criteria listed for primary acquired melanosis are no recent growth, no thickening, and involvement of less than 1/3 of bulbar conjunctiva. Features listed for a probable naevus are visible cysts, involvement confined to bulbar conjunctiva, no feeder vessels, and no growth after the second decade of life. Eyelid and orbital tumours are listed among tumours not to refer to this service; in Scotland, patients with these tumours may instead be referred to the Scottish service.

document_sections.heading: Table 1 The MOLES acronym and scoring system for categorising melanocytic choroidal tumours according to likelihood of malignancy
document_sections.content: The table sets out MOLES risk factors, severity scores, categories by total score, and suggested monitoring or referral according to estimated malignancy likelihood. DD means disc diameter (=1.5 mm). Thickness is disregarded when it cannot be measured, and definite enlargement is confirmed by sequential photography. A note states that growth is assumed when tumour diameter>5DD and/or thickness>3.0 mm and that enlargement is scored = 1; the table’s enlargement row instead places assumed enlargement with score 2.

document_sections.heading: Suspected retinoblastoma
document_sections.content: Refer urgently to a nationally designated retinoblastoma service in London or Birmingham. Email the specified contacts urgently and telephone to confirm receipt.

document_sections.heading: All other tumours
document_sections.content: Explain the differential diagnosis to the patient, why the appointment must be kept, and what to do if no letter arrives by the specified date. Review the latest guidance. Send the referral securely by electronic means, using NHS eReferral Service (eRS), or by 1st-class post, unless the patient consents to another approach. For a malignant tumour or one requiring urgent treatment, follow the NHS 2-week-wait protocol for suspected cancer. Within 24 hours of deciding to refer, confirm the referral to both the GP and patient, give the patient a telephone number to use if no appointment letter arrives in 2 weeks, and check that the hospital has received the referral. Optometrists and GPs should refer to a general ophthalmologist, not directly to an ocular oncologist.

document_sections.heading: All patients
document_sections.content: Provide the patient’s identifying and contact details, including mobile number and email address, and the names and contact details of the referrer, GP and optometrist. Include the clinical history, ophthalmic findings, relevant diagnostic reports, recent blood-test or scan results, recent lesion images obtained with colour imaging, optical coherence tomography, autofluorescence imaging or ultrasound, and the oldest available images if growth has been documented. State any special needs or preferences, such as an interpreter. Do not perform conjunctival biopsies or postpone referral for investigations. An ocular oncologist reviews every referral and may direct the patient to a virtual clinic or video or telephone consultation instead of an unnecessary in-person visit. If adequate clinical information and lesion images are missing without good reason, the centre must request them, delaying care. Ophthalmologists may refer to any centre. In Scotland, referral to a centre other than Glasgow should occur only exceptionally and after approval from National Services Division NHS Scotland.

prognostic_tools.name: MOLES
components: Mushroom shape: absent = 0; uncertain or early growth through RPE = 1; present with overhang = 2.
Orange pigment: absent = 0; uncertain or trace dusting = 1; confluent clumps = 2.
Large Size*: thickness < 1.0 mm and diameter < 3 DD = 0; thickness = 1.0 – 2.0 mm and/or diameter = 3-4 DD = 1; thickness >2.0 mm and/or diameter >4 DD = 2.

Enlargement***: none or no previous ophthalmoscopy = 0; uncertain because of poor image quality or a new lesion without an earlier photograph = 1; definite** or assumed if thickness > 3.0 mm or diameter >5DD = 2.
Subretinal fluid: absent = 0; minimal fluid detected only with OCT = 1; fluid visible without OCT or extending beyond tumour margins = 2.
prognostic_tools.interpretation: MOLES categorises lesions by likelihood of malignancy. Suggested management is community optometrist monitoring for score 0, optometrist or ophthalmologist monitoring for score 1, ophthalmologist monitoring for score 2, and urgent ocular oncologist referral for score 3. DD = disc diameter (=1.5 mm). *Thickness is disregarded if it cannot be measured. **Definite growth is confirmed by sequential photography. ***A note states that growth is assumed when tumour diameter>5DD and/or thickness>3.0 mm and assigns enlargement = 1; the table instead places assumed growth with enlargement score 2.

recommended_tests: Monitoring according to the MOLES score.

conditions.name: Choroidal haemangioma
conditions.description: Referral is indicated when subretinal fluid and/or symptoms are present; the guidance lists lesions without serous retinal detachment among those not to refer.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Symptoms and subretinal fluid are possible findings.

conditions.name: Choroidal osteoma
conditions.description: Listed among uveal tumours for referral to an ocular oncology service.

conditions.name: Lymphoma
conditions.description: Listed as a referral indication among both uveal and conjunctival or epibulbar tumours.

conditions.name: Melanocytic iris tumour
conditions.description: Referral applies if any specified size, growth, dissemination, complication or angle-involvement criterion is present.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Referral features are diameter > 5.0 mm, diffuse growth or seeding, secondary glaucoma or cataract, or angle involvement.

conditions.name: Iris cyst
conditions.description: Referral applies to a cyst that threatens vision, for example because it is large or has documented growth.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Large size or documented enlargement may indicate a threat to vision.

conditions.name: Ciliary body tumour
conditions.description: Any tumour of the ciliary body is listed for referral.

conditions.name: Metastatic or paraneoplastic tumour
conditions.description: Referral is indicated when specialist ocular oncology care is required.

conditions.name: Primary intraocular tumour
conditions.description: An unlisted primary intraocular tumour may warrant referral when an ocular oncology opinion is indicated.

conditions.name: Nodular melanocytic tumour
conditions.description: In the conjunctival and epibulbar group, referral applies when any listed location, growth, size, vascular or pigmentation feature occurs.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Referral features are non-bulbar conjunctival involvement, growth after teenage years, diameter > 5 mm, feeder vessels or diffuse pigmentation.

conditions.name: Primary acquired melanosis
conditions.description: Referral applies with recent growth, involvement of more than a third of the conjunctiva or non-bulbar involvement. The guidance lists lesions with no recent growth, no thickening and involvement of less than 1/3 of bulbar conjunctiva among those not to refer.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Recent growth, extent of conjunctival involvement, non-bulbar location and thickening are features used in the referral criteria.

conditions.name: Squamous/sebaceous carcinoma
